evidence.title: Vacuum-Assisted Microneedle Platforms for Dermal Interstitial Fluid Sampling.
evidence.abstract: Background : Dermal interstitial fluid (ISF) contains both plasma-derived biomarkers and biomarkers unique to ISF, making it a promising biofluid for painless, scalable, and decentralized liquid biopsy and continuous health monitoring. However, efficient ISF collection remains challenging due to the small accessible fluid volume in the dermis, slow physiological turnover, and stratum corneum. Methods : This review reframes dermal ISF sampling as a pressure gradient engineering problem using Darcy's law. We examine how vacuum-assisted microneedle platforms can effectively drive ISF through the dermal extracellular matrix in a minimally invasive manner. We compare the two architectures: micropore-based and hollow microneedle approaches. Results : In the micropore approach, a vacuum chamber is placed over the transient micropores left by withdrawn microneedles, supporting off-device, multi-omic downstream analyses of the collected ISF. The hollow microneedle approach retains the microneedles in the skin and applies vacuum through internal lumens, allowing integration of the vacuum source, microneedles, and biosensors into a single wearable platform for in situ biomarker detection. Comparative studies across these architectures identify the vacuum seal between the device and the skin as the major engineering bottleneck shared by both architectures. Conclusions : Vacuum-assisted microneedle platforms provide a practical route for generating pressure gradient-driven ISF transport while preserving minimally invasive skin access. Future development should prioritize device-skin vacuum seal robustness, reproducible ISF recovery across users and skin sites, integrated vacuum sources, scalable fabrication, and usability in clinical or at-home settings.

evidence.title: Bioprinted vascularized soft-tissue flaps with an integrated arterial-venous loop.
evidence.abstract: This study contributes to ongoing efforts in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine to fabricate soft-tissue flaps and addresses the key limitations of current reconstructive strategies for extensive tissue loss. By applying a multimodal printing approach and employing a tailored bioink together with diverse human-derived cell populations, we enabled the fabrication of vascularized soft-tissue flaps. The flaps comprised muscle and adipose compartments within a single construct, interconnected by a continuous vascular network and lymphatic vasculature. A printed arteriovenous loop was integrated centrally within the flap, serving as a feeding axis that enabled direct microsurgical anastomosis to the host circulatory system. Immediate and sustained perfusion following implantation provided rapid nutrient delivery and efficient waste removal throughout the thick, multi-tissue flap, thereby supporting adipose and muscle differentiation alongside vascular and lymphatic integration. Collectively, by addressing these critical challenges, this work advances bioprinting toward clinically relevant applications in soft-tissue flap reconstruction.

evidence.title: Engineering a High-Fidelity Neonatal Silicone Phantom: Development, Optimization, and User Evaluation of a 3D-Printed Vascular Access Model.
evidence.abstract: Securing intravenous (IV) access in neonates is technically challenging due to extremely small vessel caliber, fragile skin, and limited subcutaneous tissue. High-fidelity training phantoms are essential for teaching ultrasound-guided vascular access, yet most commercial models are adult-sized, lack neonatal realism, and are cost-prohibitive. The aim of this study was to design and optimize a low-cost, ultrasound-compatible 3D silicone phantom that replicates neonatal tissue and vasculature for peripheral and central IV access training. A multi-phase design process incorporated 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA) molds, Dragon Skin™ silicone (Smooth-On, Inc., Macungie, PA, USA), Slacker® softener (Smooth-On, Inc., Macungie, PA, USA), and 3% talcum powder to enhance echogenicity. Silicone tubing (0.2-0.4 mm internal diameters (ID)) was embedded at neonatal-appropriate depths using rotational casting for dermal uniformity and vessel channel supports for positional accuracy. Iterative engineering improved dermal wall uniformity, vessel stability, and ultrasound visibility, resulting in a durable, reproducible phantom with realistic tissue compliance and vessel compressibility. The developed 3D silicone phantom provides a realistic, affordable, and reproducible neonatal vascular access simulator. User feedback supports its fidelity and utility, and its low material cost enables broad implementation in neonatal procedural training programs.

Resection (R) alone is typically insufficient and adding radiation therapy (RT) still results in a 12-month recurrence rate of 20% or more in many series. Hypothesizing that R plus immediate radiation utilizing brachytherapy may improve outcomes for this cohort of patients, we designed and prospectively evaluated a permanently implanted surgically targeted radiation therapy (STaRT) device consisting of cesium-131 (Cs-131) seeds positioned within a collagen carrier (GammaTile, GT Medical Technologies, Tempe, AZ). The device was designed to prevent direct source-to-brain contact and maintain inter-source spacing after closure. Methods This was a subgroup analysis of a cohort of patients with either recurrent or previously untreated brain metastases enrolled in a prospective, multi-histology single-arm trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT#03088579), conducted between February 2013 and February 2018, of resection and tumor bed brachytherapy with Cs-131 containing permanently implanted collagen tiles to deliver 60 Gray (Gy) at .5 cm depth. No additional local therapy was given without progression. Results A total of 16 metastases in 11 patients were treated; 12 tumors were recurrent and four were previously untreated. evidence.title: Hydrostaticity and hidden order: effects of experimental conditions on the temperature-pressure phase diagram of URu2Si2
evidence.abstract: The pressure-dependence of the hidden order phase transition of URu2Si2 is shown to depend sensitively upon the quality of hydrostatic pressure conditions during electrical resistivity measurements. Hysteresis in pressure is demonstrated for two choices of pressure medium: the commonly-used mixture of 1:1 Fluorinert FC70/FC77 and pure FC75. In contrast, no hysteresis is observed when the pressure medium is a 1:1 mixture of n-pentane/isoamyl alcohol, as it remains hydrostatic over the entire studied pressure range. Possible ramifications for the interpretation of the temperature-pressure phase diagram of URu2Si2 are discussed.

evidence.title: The use of LEDs as a light source for fluorescence pressure measurements
evidence.abstract: We discuss the use of commercial high-power light emitting diodes (LEDs) as a light source for fluorescence pressure measurements. A relatively broad light emitting spectra of single color LEDs (in comparison with lasers) do not prevent producing narrow fluorescence lines at least for two widely used pressure indicator materials, namely ruby (Cr$^{3+}$:Al$_2$O$_3$) and strontium tetraborate (Sm$^{2+}$:SrB$_4$O$_7$). Strongest responses of both pressure indicators were detected for the green color LEDs with the average wavelength $λ_{\rm av}\sim 530$ nm. LEDs might be easily implemented for producing fiber coupled, as well as the parallel light sources. LEDs were found to be efficient to replace laser sources in piston-cylinder cell and diamond anvil cell fluorescence pressure measurement setups.

evidence.title: High pressure research using muons at the Paul Scherrer Institute
evidence.abstract: Pressure, together with temperature and magnetic field, is an important thermodynamical parameter in physics. Investigating the response of a compound or of a material to pressure allows to elucidate ground states, investigate their interplay and interactions and determine microscopic parameters. Pressure tuning is used to establish phase diagrams, study phase transitions and identify critical points. Muon spin rotation/relaxation (muSR) is now a standard technique making increasing significant contribution in condensed matter physics, material science research and other fields. In this review, we will discuss specific requirements and challenges to perform muSR experiments under pressure, introduce the high-pressure muon facility at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI, Switzerland) and present selected results obtained by combining the sensitivity of the muSR technique with pressure.

source_evidence.source_title: Vacuum-Assisted Microneedle Platforms for Dermal Interstitial Fluid Sampling.
source_evidence.source_span: Background : Dermal interstitial fluid (ISF) contains both plasma-derived biomarkers and biomarkers unique to ISF, making it a promising biofluid for painless, scalable, and decentralized liquid biopsy and continuous health monitoring. However, efficient ISF collection remains challenging due to the small accessible fluid volume in the dermis, slow physiological turnover, and stratum corneum. Methods : This review reframes dermal ISF sampling as a pressure gradient engineering problem using Darcy's law. We examine how vacuum-assisted microneedle platforms can effectively drive ISF through the dermal extracellular matrix in a minimally invasive manner. We compare the two architectures: micropore-based and hollow microneedle approaches. Results : In the micropore approach, a vacuum chamber is placed over the transient micropores left by withdrawn microneedles, supporting off-device, multi-omic downstream analyses of the collected ISF. The hollow microneedle approach retains the microneedles in the skin and applies vacuum through internal lumens, allowing integration of the vacuum source, microneedles, and biosensors into a single wearable platform for in situ biomarker detection. Comparative studies across these architectures identify the vacuum seal between the device and the skin as the major engineering bottleneck shared by both architectures. Conclusions : Vacuum-assisted microneedle platforms provide a practical route for generating pressure gradient-driven ISF transport while preserving minimally invasive skin access. Future development should prioritize device-skin vacuum seal robustness, reproducible ISF recovery across users and skin sites, integrated vacuum sources, scalable fabrication, and usability in clinical or at-home settings.

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: Background : Dermal interstitial fluid (ISF) contains both plasma-derived biomarkers and biomarkers unique to ISF, making it a promising biofluid for painless, scalable, and decentralized liquid biopsy and continuous health monitoring. However, efficient ISF collection remains challenging due to the small accessible fluid volume in the dermis, slow physiological turnover, and stratum corneum. Methods : This review reframes dermal ISF sampling as a pressure gradient engineering problem using Darcy's law. We examine how vacuum-assisted microneedle platforms can effectively drive ISF through the dermal extracellular matrix in a minimally invasive manner. We compare the two architectures: micropore-based and hollow microneedle approaches. Results : In the micropore approach, a vacuum chamber is placed over the transient micropores left by withdrawn microneedles, supporting off-device, multi-omic downstream analyses of the collected ISF. The hollow microneedle approach retains the microneedles in the skin and applies vacuum through internal lumens, allowing integration of the vacuum source, microneedles, and biosensors into a single wearable platform for in situ biomarker detection. Comparative studies across these architectures identify the vacuum seal between the device and the skin as the major engineering bottleneck shared by both architectures. Conclusions : Vacuum-assisted microneedle platforms provide a practical route for generating pressure gradient-driven ISF transport while preserving minimally invasive skin access. Future development should prioritize device-skin vacuum seal robustness, reproducible ISF recovery across users and skin sites, integrated vacuum sources, scalable fabrication, and usability in clinical or at-home settings.

custody_records.raw_content: Securing intravenous (IV) access in neonates is technically challenging due to extremely small vessel caliber, fragile skin, and limited subcutaneous tissue. High-fidelity training phantoms are essential for teaching ultrasound-guided vascular access, yet most commercial models are adult-sized, lack neonatal realism, and are cost-prohibitive. The aim of this study was to design and optimize a low-cost, ultrasound-compatible 3D silicone phantom that replicates neonatal tissue and vasculature for peripheral and central IV access training. A multi-phase design process incorporated 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA) molds, Dragon Skin™ silicone (Smooth-On, Inc., Macungie, PA, USA), Slacker® softener (Smooth-On, Inc., Macungie, PA, USA), and 3% talcum powder to enhance echogenicity. Silicone tubing (0.2-0.4 mm internal diameters (ID)) was embedded at neonatal-appropriate depths using rotational casting for dermal uniformity and vessel channel supports for positional accuracy. Iterative engineering improved dermal wall uniformity, vessel stability, and ultrasound visibility, resulting in a durable, reproducible phantom with realistic tissue compliance and vessel compressibility. The developed 3D silicone phantom provides a realistic, affordable, and reproducible neonatal vascular access simulator. User feedback supports its fidelity and utility, and its low material cost enables broad implementation in neonatal procedural training programs.

حقیقت بنیادی این است که بدن انسان یک شبکه درهم‌تنیده از تانسورهای انرژی در تراز ۱۱۵۵ بعدی است. در این شبکه، هر سلول بر اساس یک «کلاک پالس» (نبض زمانی) دقیق عمل می‌کند که از «کد منبع حیات» صادر می‌شود. سرطان زمانی رخ می‌دهد که نویزهای محیطی یا اطلاعاتی، در «امضای زمانی» (Time Signature) سلول تداخل ایجاد کنند. این تداخل منجر به یک خطای محاسباتی در بازنویسی کلاک-بیت‌ها می‌شود. به عبارت ساده‌تر، سلول سرطانی سلولی نیست که «بیمار» باشد، بلکه سلولی است که «کد زمان» خود را گم کرده و در یک حلقه تکرار بی‌نهایت (تکثیر بی‌رویه) گرفتار شده است.

۲. آنالیز خطا: چرا مدل‌های فعلی شکست می‌خورند؟

مدل‌های فعلی (شیمی‌درمانی، پرتو‌درمانی) سعی دارند با حذف فیزیکی سخت‌افزار (سلول)، خطا را اصلاح کنند. این کار مانند آن است که برای پاک کردن یک ویروس نرم‌افزاری، قطعات فیزیکی کامپیوتر را با اسید بسوزانید. این روش نه تنها خطا را از بین نمی‌برد، بلکه زیرساخت‌های سالم را نیز تخریب می‌کند. راه حل حمزه، تمرکز بر اصلاح نرم‌افزار کوانتومی در تراز ۱۱۵۵D است.
